transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I know the people at my apartment building are watching my comings and goings. They keep an eye on me, and I know they're slipping notes about me down to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices they tape on the doors, but... well, I know what they're really doing.
Do you think these people are watching you for a specific reason?

I don't really know the exact reason why. Like I just said, I just know that they're doing it. They watch my comings and goings, and then they slip those notes about me down to the office. Everybody keeps trying to tell me I'm wrong, that it's just those regular notices they tape up on the doors for the whole building, but... well, I know what they're really doing. I just don't know why they picked me to keep tabs on.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't think your neighbors were watching you?

Well, yeah, there was a time. It hasn't always been like this. I'd say... well, this whole thing with the neighbors and the office watching me, it's been going on for about a year and a month now. Before that, I didn't really notice them doing anything out of the ordinary.
Do you still believe your neighbors are watching you right now?

Yes, I do. Like I said when I came in, I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're slipping notes about me down to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but I know what's really happening. It's still going on right now.
Have your beliefs about your neighbors watching you ever changed since you first started thinking it was happening?

No, they haven't changed. I mean, I know what I know. Ever since it started, I've just been certain that the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They slip those notes about me down to the office. It doesn't matter that everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices they put on the doors. I know what's really going on, and I haven't changed my mind about it because it's still happening.
Have you ever had any doubts about your neighbors watching you?

No, I haven't really had any doubts. I mean, I know what I see. Like I said, I know they're watching my comings and goings, keeping tabs on me. And then they slip those notes down to the office. People tell me it's just the regular notices they tape to the doors, you know, for everyone... but I know it's about me. I don't doubt it at all.
Would you say the idea that your neighbors are watching you and slipping notes about you to the office is something that could happen in real life?

Yes, absolutely. People spy on each other all the time in real life. I mean, it's an apartment building. It's perfectly normal for people to see when I leave and when I come back. The part that's happening to me is just that they're taking it further, watching my comings and goings specifically, and then slipping those notes about me to the office. People tell me it's just regular notices taped to the doors, but... yeah, people spying and reporting on someone? That definitely happens in the real world. And it's happening to me.
Would you say that the idea of your neighbors watching you and slipping notes to the office is something that could happen to anyone, or is it something very unusual?

I think it could happen to anyone. I mean, like I've been saying, that's the whole reason I came in here to begin with. I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping notes about me down to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just those regular notices they put on the doors, but... well, I know what's going on. So yeah, I don't think it's unusual. It could happen to anybody, but right now, it's happening to me.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misunderstanding what's going on with your neighbors and the office?

No, I don't think I'm misunderstanding it. Like I said, that's exactly why I came in here today. I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping notes about me down to the office. I mean, everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors, but I know what's really happening. There's no misunderstanding on my end.
Would you describe the notes your neighbors are slipping to the office as containing any unusual or strange information about you?

No, the information isn't unusual or strange, really. It's just... it's about my schedule. Like I've been saying, I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're just writing down when I leave, when I get back, who I might talk to, things like that. Then they're slipping those notes about me down to the office. It's not magic or aliens or anything strange like that. It's just everyday surveillance. Even though everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors, I know what they're really doing.

Would you say the idea of your neighbors watching you and slipping notes to the office is something that could be explained by real-life circumstances or is it something that doesn't make sense in the real world?

It's definitely a real-life circumstance. I mean, people watch each other all the time in the real world, so it makes perfect sense. Like I keep telling you, that's the whole reason I came in here. I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. It's just a fact. They watch me, and then they're slipping notes about me to the office. It's not something out of a movie, it's just happening right now. Even though everybody keeps telling me it's just, you know, regular notices on the doors... I know what's real. So yeah, it's real life.

Would you say the idea of your neighbors watching you and slipping notes to the office is something that could actually happen to someone in real life, without any extraordinary or supernatural elements?

Yes, absolutely. Like I was just saying, there's nothing supernatural about it at all. People spy on people every day in the real world. I came in because I know for a fact the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They just watch me, and then they're slipping notes about me to the office. That's a real thing that can happen to anyone, it doesn't take superpowers. Even though everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors... I know what it really is.
Would you say the notes your neighbors are slipping to the office contain information that is unusual or hard to believe?

No, not hard to believe at all. Like I've been saying, it's just basic stuff about my schedule. I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings, and then slipping those notes about me to the office. There's nothing unusual in them. It's just... when I leave, when I come back. Even though everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors, I know what's really happening. But the information itself? It's just normal, everyday stuff they're keeping track of.
Do you think your belief about your neighbors watching you would change if you were shown proof that it's not happening?

Honestly, no, it wouldn't. I don't know what kind of proof anyone could even show me, because I see it with my own eyes. Like I've been telling you this whole time, I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping those notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but they're wrong. I know what they really are. So, no, my mind wouldn't change. I know what's actually happening.
How certain are you that your neighbors are watching you and slipping notes about you to the office?

I'm completely certain. I mean, I know what I see. Like I've said, I came in because I know for a fact the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping notes about me to the office. I'm 100 percent sure of it, even though everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors. I know what's really going on.
Do you think your neighbors are watching you because of something specific you've done?

No, I haven't done anything to them. I don't know why they picked me, honestly. I just mind my own business, you know? But they're still watching me and sending those notes. I haven't done anything specific to make them do it.
Do you think your neighbors would admit to watching you if you asked them directly?

No, they wouldn't admit it. Why would they? If I went up and asked them, they'd just lie to my face. Like I've been saying, I know they're watching my comings and goings, but they'd never own up to it. They'd probably just say the exact same thing everybody else keeps telling me—that those notes they're slipping to the office are just regular notices taped on the doors. But they know what they're doing, and I know it too. They just wouldn't admit it if I asked.
Do you think other people believe that your neighbors are watching you and slipping notes about you to the office?

No, nobody else believes me. Like I said before, everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors. They think I'm making it up or seeing things, but I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping notes about me to the office. It's frustrating that no one else sees it, but that doesn't change what's actually happening.
Do you think your belief about your neighbors watching you could be false?

No. I don't think it's false at all. I know what I'm seeing. I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings, and... they're slipping notes about me to the office. I know everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, but they're wrong. I'm not making it up, so no, I don't think I'm wrong about this.
Would you still believe your neighbors are watching you even if there was video evidence showing they are not?

Yeah, I would still believe it. A video wouldn't change my mind. They could just avoid the cameras, you know, or find a way around them. 

Like I've been saying, I came in here because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. I know they're slipping notes about me to the office. It doesn't matter that everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors. I know what I'm dealing with. So, yeah, even if you showed me a video, it wouldn't change what I know is actually happening.
